Vicenza S.p.A.''' (acronym for ''Lanerossi Vicenza''), better known as '''Vicenza''' or '''Lanerossi''', is an Italian football club based in the city of [[Vicenza]]. It plays in [[Serie C]], the third division of the Italian football league, but will play in [[Serie B]] in the [[2026–27 Serie B|2026–27 season]] following promotion. Founded on 9 March 1902, as ''Associazione del Calcio in Vicenza'', it is the oldest football club in north-eastern Italy as well as in the [[Triveneto]] and [[Veneto]] regions. It has competed in 30 [[Serie A]] seasons and is listed by the [[IFFHS]] as the 15 best Italian teams of the 20th century. Domestically, Vicenza won the [[Coppa Italia]] in 1996–1997 and the [[Coppa Italia Serie C|Italian Cup Serie C]] in 1981–1982 and 2022–2023, while its best result at international level is reaching the semi-final of the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] (1997–1998). It reached the final in the 1910–1911 First Division championship, where it was defeated by [[FC Pro Vercelli 1892|Pro Vercelli]], and finished as runners-up [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the 1977–1978 [[Serie A]] championship, in which it achieved the best result ever by a newly promoted club in the single-round era. The club was reformed in 2018, following Vicenza Calcio's bankruptcy, thanks to the moving and name change of ''[[Bassano Virtus 55 ST|Bassano Virtus]]'' (then owned by [[OTB Group]]) from [[Bassano del Grappa|Bassano]] to Vicenza. L.R Vicenza is now the heir, and ''de facto'' continuation, of the sporting tradition that began on 9 March 1902 with the founding of ''Associazione del Calcio in Vicenza'' which later became ''Lanerossi Vicenza'' from 1953 to 1989 and finally ''Vicenza Calcio'', before going bankrupt in 2018."}}
